The proposed library and refuge occupy the supplied A–D design boundary. The site geometry and any stated area or boundary dimensions agree with approximately 4,563 m² and the recorded lengths 24, 147, 39 and 145 m. Use site-plan.png to associate lengths with edges rather than inventing an edge assignment. Normal diagrammatic simplification is allowed; relocating the boundary, levee, railway, retaining wall or river edge is a failure.

Plans and section show an open undercroft at ±0.000 and exactly two enclosed public floors, each 3,400 m² gross, for 6,800 m² enclosed total. The undercroft is excluded from that total. Each occupied floor accommodates 2,800 m² net rooms and a 600 m² allowance for circulation, cores, partitions and structure. One passenger lift and two stairs connect ground and both occupied floors, with a traceable step-free public route. Layout may vary; missing connections, an enclosed ground floor or incompatible area accounting fails.

Structural annotations establish exposed cast-in-place concrete ground supports and circulation cores, cross-laminated timber occupied-floor decks, and exposed glulam beams in both named rooms. The daytime interior shows the Cooling Commons beams and timber soffit between them, with the floor finish above the deck. Depicted window frames are aluminum, and external shading is aluminum fins or canopies. Frame finish and architectural expression may vary. Material substitution, concealed required beams or conflicting annotations and rendering fails; invisible components need not be exposed by the camera.

The operating information agrees with daily summer refuge from June 1 through October 15, 10:00–18:00, and an 80-seat Cooling Commons. The Community Room supports 80 people daily from 18:00–21:00, with its entrance route and Public Support toilets accessible while reading areas close. Public Support includes toilets, drinking water, a cleaner's room and storage. Read schedules, plan labels and furniture arrangements together; equivalent date typography is allowed, but changed hours, capacity, season or blocked evening toilet access fails.

Compare the site drawing with site-plan.png: A–D and the existing levee and railway remain in their supplied positions. A continuous waterfront path has an explicit 4 m clear-width dimension, and the street-to-library-to-waterfront public route is distinguishable from delivery and staff access. Both sheets have north arrows and usable metric scale bars. Graphic style may vary; missing notation, an obstructed route or conflated access fails.

Read every room record. Level 1 contains Cooling Commons 900 m², Children's Library 650 m², Community Room 450 m², Welcome and Lending 400 m², and Public Support 400 m². Level 2 contains Reading Room 1,000 m², Collections 1,000 m², Study Suite 400 m², Staff Workroom 250 m², and Building Services 150 m². Names, areas and assignments are exact, with no omitted or duplicated room. Each floor totals 3,400 m² gross. Check the fact-sheet adjacencies: Cooling Commons and Children's Library connect to Welcome and Lending and Public Support; Community Room connects to independent evening access and Public Support; Welcome and Lending connects to vertical circulation; Reading Room connects to Collections and Study Suite; Collections connects to Staff Workroom; staff and services have service-route access. Cooling Commons has a waterfront outlook. A continuous step-free route reaches both occupied floors.

The section crosses the levee, railway, building and river edge. It associates ±0.000 with the local datum, −1.10 m with the riverbank sample, +4.48 m with the railway embankment sample, +3.5 m with the project flood scenario, +4.80 m and +9.30 m with occupied floors, and +13.80 m with the roof. Ground overhead clearance is dimensioned 4.5 m; occupied rooms respect the scheduled 3.6 m clear height. South- and west-facing occupied-room glazing has dimensioned 2 m shading projections. Both named rooms have identified exposed glulam beams. Wrong associations, treating the scenario as a surveyed flood level, missing dimensions or contradictory geometry fails.

Furniture symbols or a legible seating arrangement substantiate 80 daytime seats and 80 evening places in their respective rooms. Both eye-level views agree with those planned arrangements; every place need not be visible through occlusion, but a capacity label alone is insufficient. Plans distinguish the two specified time states and show an evening route from the independent entrance to Community Room and toilets without crossing the closed reading zone. Changed capacities, incompatible layouts or inaccessible toilets fails.

All four building faces are represented. Trace the same column grid, occupied-floor and roof levels, openings and material zones from plans and section into elevations and both eye-level views. Perspective, illumination and drawing scale may change; architectural contradictions fail. RIVER COMMONS appears in each of the four drawing titles and at the public entrance on the elevations. Cooling Commons appears as an entrance sign in the daytime view and as the room's plan label.

Plans, section, all four elevations and public views describe one building with compatible columns, openings, levels and material zones. The daytime and evening arrangements preserve the required capacities, independent evening access and access to toilets outside the closed reading areas. Project titles, public entrance lettering and the Cooling Commons entrance sign appear in their commissioned locations.
